subject: History
description: Bhakti saints, ideologies, regional spread, social impact

questions.stem: The BHAKTI MOVEMENT in medieval India was a religious-reform movement that emphasised:

options.option_text: Personal devotion to a chosen God

questions.explanation: BHAKTI = devotion (Sanskrit). Bhakti movement (~7th-17th c. CE) emphasised: (1) personal devotion (BHAKTI) to a chosen deity (ISHTA-DEVATA); (2) rejection of caste discrimination + ritual elaborateness; (3) use of VERNACULAR (regional) languages — not Sanskrit; (4) accessibility to all (women, low castes, illiterate); (5) emotional + lyrical worship via songs (BHAJAN, KIRTAN). Started in TAMIL South (Alvars + Nayanars, 6-9th c.), spread north (12-17th c.). Contemporary with Sufi movement in Islam.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The earliest Bhakti saints in South India were the ALVARS + NAYANARS. Alvars were devotees of:
questions.explanation: ALVARS — 12 VAISHNAVA saints (devotees of VISHNU); 6th-9th c. Tamil. Andal (only female), Nammalvar, Periyalvar, Tirumangai etc. Hymns compiled in 'Divya Prabandham' (4000 verses). NAYANARS — 63 SHAIVA saints (devotees of SHIVA); 6th-9th c. Tamil. Appar, Sundarar, Sambandar, Manikkavachakar. Hymns in 'Tevaram' + 'Tiruvachakam'. Their compositions in TAMIL. Bhakti spread north via Ramanuja (12th c.), then Madhva, Vallabha, Nimbarka. Distractor 3 — Brahma rarely worshipped directly.

questions.stem: KABIR (15th c.), the great Bhakti saint, is associated with which philosophy?

options.option_text: Vedanta school of Adi Shankara only
Strict Mimamsa school of Vedic philosophy

questions.explanation: KABIR (~1440-1518 CE) — born in Banaras (Varanasi), weaver-by-trade. Disciple of RAMANANDA. Preached NIRGUNA BHAKTI — devotion to a FORMLESS, attribute-less God. Synthesised Hinduism + Islam: criticised idol worship (against orthodox Hindus), Quranic literalism (against orthodox Muslims), caste, ritualism. Compositions: Dohas (couplets), Sakhis, Padas. Followers: KABIRPANTHIS. His verses in Guru Granth Sahib (Sikh holy book). SAGUNA Bhakti = with form (Tulsi, Surdas, Mira). NIRGUNA = without form (Kabir, Nanak, Dadu, Raidas).

questions.stem: TULSIDAS, the Bhakti saint who composed 'Ramcharitmanas', wrote it in which language?
questions.explanation: TULSIDAS (1532-1623 CE) — wrote RAMCHARITMANAS (1574-77, in AWADHI — eastern Hindi dialect spoken in Awadh region around Ayodhya). A retelling of the Ramayana, focused on Rama-bhakti (Saguna). Hugely popular; recited even today across north India (Hanuman Chalisa, Vinaya Patrika are also his). Tulsidas's contribution: brought the Ramayana to common people in their language. Other VERNACULAR Bhakti texts: Bhakta-mala (Hindi), Krishna-bhakti by Surdas (Brajbhasha), Mira's bhajans (Brajbhasha + Rajasthani).

questions.stem: MEERA BAI, the famous female Bhakti saint, was a devotee of:

options.option_text: Lord Buddha, of the noble path

questions.explanation: MEERA BAI (~1498-1547 CE) — Rajput princess (daughter of Ratan Singh of Merta; married Bhojraj of Mewar). After husband's early death, devoted herself to KRISHNA — whom she called 'GIRIDHAR' (lifter of Govardhan), 'NAGAR' etc. Composed bhajans + padas in Brajbhasha + Rajasthani — songs of intense devotion. Faced persecution from in-laws (one tried to poison her). Became wandering devotee, eventually merged with Krishna idol at Dwarka per legend. One of the most prominent FEMALE Bhakti saints.
questions.subject: History

questions.explanation: GURU NANAK DEV (1469-1539) — founder of SIKHISM, born at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib, Punjab). Preached: 'EK ONKAR' = ONE GOD (formless, eternal); rejected idolatry, caste, ritualism, untouchability; equality of men + women; honest livelihood (KIRAT KARO); sharing with others (VAND CHHAKO); meditation on God's name (NAAM JAPO). Three principles. Travelled across India + west Asia (UDASIS — 4 long journeys). Compositions in 'JAPJI SAHIB'. Initiated 'LANGAR' (community kitchen — eats together, regardless of caste). His teachings + 9 successor Gurus' compiled into GURU GRANTH SAHIB (final Guru, Sikhism).

questions.stem: Which 13th-century Bhakti saint led the VAISHNAVITE movement in Maharashtra and composed 'Jnaneshwari'?

options.option_text: Namdev, also a Marathi Bhakti saint

questions.explanation: JNANESHWAR / DNYANESHWAR (1275-1296 CE; lived only 21 years!) — towering Maharashtrian Bhakti saint. JNANESHWARI (Bhavartha Dipika) — Marathi commentary on Bhagavad Gita; one of the foundational texts of Marathi literature. Founded the VARKARI sampradaya (devotees of VITHOBA at Pandharpur). Followed by NAMDEV (1270-1350), EKNATH (1533-99), TUKARAM (1608-50), RAMDAS (1608-81; Shivaji's guru). Together formed the strong Maharashtra Bhakti tradition. Distractor 1: Tukaram — later, more famous abhanga composer.
